name: Quoridor 4x7, 7 walls per player: exact initial outcome
compute_profile: laptop-hours (HEURISTIC scouting budget only; target runtime and memory unmeasured. Measure a small calibration sequentially, then use a time cap, checkpoints and the charter memory limit; no promise that a laptop can finish.)
statement: KNOWN (source definition): Grant Slatton's rectangular Quoridor variant at commit fe2a222f474c55e811c946594bbf7c62d90daa81. Coordinates are (row,column), zero-based; width W counts columns and height H counts rows. Player 1 starts at (0,floor(W/2)), Player 2 at (H-1,floor(W/2)); Player 1 moves first and aims for row H-1, Player 2 for row 0. Initially no wall is placed. Each turn moves the current pawn or spends one wall from that player's supply. An ordinary pawn move follows one orthogonal unblocked edge to an empty cell. If the adjacent cell holds the opponent, and the edge to that cell is clear, jump straight over when the next cell and edge exist and are clear. Only when that straight jump is blocked by a wall or boundary may the pawn land in either perpendicular neighbour of the opponent, provided that edge is clear. Walls are permanent. A horizontal wall H(r,c), with 0<=r<H-1 and 0<=c<W-1, blocks edges (r,c)--(r+1,c) and (r,c+1)--(r+1,c+1). A vertical wall V(r,c) blocks (r,c)--(r,c+1) and (r+1,c)--(r+1,c+1). Opposite orientations at the same anchor cross and cannot coexist. Horizontal walls overlap when their rows agree and columns differ by at most one; vertical walls overlap when their columns agree and rows differ by at most one. Reject all crossing or overlapping placements. After placement, both pawns must have a path through unblocked orthogonal edges to their own goal row, ignoring pawn occupancy for this test. Reaching a goal ends play immediately. There is no pass or repetition-count cutoff. Infinite play is a draw; a non-goal state with no successor is treated as a draw, matching the source retrograde semantics. The question is the exact initial outcome under optimal play (win preferred to draw preferred to loss). Fixed target: W=4, H=7, 7 initial walls per player. KNOWN (table snapshot): this exact cell is marked ? in the pinned README. This means uncomputed by that source, not proven absent from all literature. Status evidence retrieved 2026-11-02 UTC.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED: determine exactly the initial outcome of W=4, H=7, 7 walls per player under the rules in statement, with the independently checked winning DAG or pair of non-losing draw graphs specified in verification_method. One cell per claim. Before hunting and before claiming, recheck the live source and repository for an already published outcome for this same instance; an already public value is calibration, not a new result. A timeout, heuristic score or repeated position is not a draw proof.
verification_method: Supply a standalone verifier with independently implemented rules and the exact initial state. For a claimed winner P, provide a strategy DAG rooted at the initial state: at P-to-move nodes include a legal selected successor, at opponent-to-move nodes include every legal successor; all leaves must be terminal wins for P. Include nonnegative ranks strictly decreasing on every edge to rule out cycling. For a draw, provide two non-losing strategy graphs, one for each player: each includes the root; on the protected player's turn choose a legal successor in the graph; on the other player's turn include every legal successor. No included terminal state may be a loss for the protected player. A non-goal zero-successor state is a draw leaf. Cycles are allowed in these safety graphs. These two graphs establish that neither player can force a win. The verifier regenerates all moves, validates full states, supply conservation, edges, closure, terminal labels and ranks without trusting solver hashes or evaluations. Include verifier source, certificate bytes and reproduction commands. If a certificate exceeds 1 MB, keep it outside git, give its SHA-256 and accessible location plus deterministic generation instructions; a digest alone is insufficient. Before evaluating the target, freeze and reproduce this representative pinned-README suite with both the producer and an independent rules implementation: (W,H,walls-per-player)->outcome: (2,3,0)->Player2, (2,3,1)->Player1, (4,3,0)->Player2, (4,3,3)->Player1, (4,7,2)->Player1, (4,7,3)->Player2, (8,3,3)->Draw. Include rule fixtures for straight jumps, boundary/wall-blocked jump sidesteps, overlapping/crossing walls, path-blocking illegal walls, immediate goals, and the exact even-width starting column; retain expected and actual outputs. Full-table reproduction is optional additional calibration, not a prerequisite. Calibration is not a win. Resource failure or disagreement leaves the claim unconfirmed. Any resulting claim requires the repository's three fresh-context skeptic passes and check_run gate. Strategy-choice and universal-closure obligations apply only to nonterminal nodes; terminal nodes have no outgoing edges. This fixed calibration suite is a deliberate local requirement, not a bank rule. Resource exhaustion on calibration leaves this proposal unready for a research claim; do not silently skip fixtures.
angles: HEURISTIC: finite-depth reachability proof search can produce a winning DAG; exact retrograde analysis can produce draw safety graphs. Apply only sound pruning and retain proof witnesses.
HEURISTIC: compare lazy wall-legality BFS against precomputed wall reachability after measuring memory.
pitfalls: The paper by Marius Drop, Benjamin G. Rin and Finn van der Velde supplies general Quoridor rules; Grant Slatton supplies the rectangular instance convention and table. Do not attribute the frontier to the paper.
All wall counts are per player; preserve side to move, pawn coordinates and remaining wall supplies in every state.
For even widths use floor(W/2), not the other central square or a silently rotated start.
A depth limit does not establish a draw; win certificates require a well-founded rank and draw certificates require both safety strategies.
No known-result partial wins or unspecified alternate boards are accepted. Tractability is a guess.
